A memorable hotel stay is often a matter of keeping guests’ memories in check, and that is what drew her to hotel management. Inspired by family and colleagues, she began her career in the field by completing a bachelor’s degree at a university not listed in the major global rankings, and since then, she has strengthened her commitment to guest satisfaction, operational efficiency, and leadership in hospitality. That commitment became a natural progression for her as a Senior Project Manager at a large international hotel chain, where she steadily built her skills and understanding of hotel operations while also building a strong foundation in project management.

What drew you to hotel management? My interest in hospitality began at a family-run hotel in Ethiopia, where I was taught how to run a restaurant and how to manage the kitchen team. As a family, family-run hotel management was always a natural fit, and I was encouraged to keep learning and growing as a manager. Over time, I developed a practical, operational framework for hotel operations that has helped keep guests’ memories in check, and I have completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes. In addition, I have strengthened my understanding of hotel operations by completing a practical, repeatable, and repeatable process for rostering and guest check-in, and I have been able to use it to help manage a busy hotel team while maintaining a consistent guest experience.

What keeps you consistently focused? My most rewarding part of the job is when guests leave a hotel feeling genuinely cared for, and that is what keeps me motivated. When family and colleagues visit a hotel, they often ask how we can help them feel the same way. Colle and staff have also been encouraged to use the hotel’ side of hospitality to help guests feel more at home, and I have been able to help them understand how to use the kitchen team’s skills to deliver a consistently high guest experience.

One of the most rewarding aspects of my career is the opportunity to work with a purpose-driven organisation that values collaboration, growth, and the ability to make a difference. Few roles combine science, care, and reassurance as directly as pharmacy, and that is precisely what draws her to the profession. Originally from Peru, she grew up in a family of pharmacists and healthcare professionals, and her interest in the science and everyday work of dispensing care has been strengthened by her work in patient safety. That interest continues in her work as a Pharmacist, where she brings clear understanding of the complex interactions between patient safety and patient care. Originally from Peru, she holds a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100, and her work as a Practising Pharmacist has strengthened by practical application of new medication routines and safer patient communication.

In my professional journey, I have completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, each building confidence in the science behind the dispensing of medication and demonstrating how it can improve patient care. In one project, I needed to administer a new medication routine that took months to master, and I was surprised that the patient would be reluctant to ask for help. In another, I needed to use a new tool to help me manage a recurring problem, and I was surprised that the process was simple enough for a patient to understand. Colleagues have also often come to me with questions in my own work, and I value the opportunity to help them understand the science behind the dispensing of medication safely and effectively.

I am drawn to this role because I value the reassurance and reassurance that a safe and effective dispensing of medication can bring. I am particularly drawn to the moment when a patient asks for help, and I value the opportunity to explain the science behind the process so that they can understand how it can improve their care.

What first held my attention about web development was the way a simple idea could become something useful, interactive, and accessible on a screen. That blend of creativity and logic is still what drives me: I enjoy turning complex user needs into smooth digital experiences that make everyday tasks easier. Over time, this interest grew into a wider fascination with how websites and applications are structured, improved, and used in real life. I am now seeking to build my career as a Web Developer because it brings together my interest in building practical digital products with my focus on clean, user-friendly solutions, strong front-end development, performance, and usability. Currently, I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work and study I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my commitment to creating web experiences that are functional, scalable, and intuitive.

My approach to work has been shaped by practical experience. In one role, I needed to use a new tool that was central to the team’s workflow, and after a few months of focused effort I was contributing independently to day-to-day tasks with it. On another project, a recurring issue was slowing the team down, so I put together a workable alternative process that reduced the disruption and helped us keep delivery moving. Colleagues have also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, including asking me to look over front-end implementation choices or help untangle smaller technical issues during active work. I am originally from Ethiopia, and alongside my professional goals I value the personal side of building technology. One of my favourite memories is showing my family a website I had built for a local business and watching them excitedly place a test order just to see it work in real time. That moment stayed with me because it captured exactly why I want to keep building for the web: every line of code should lead to a clear, useful experience for real people.

Nothing is more satisfying to me than restoring something essential and seeing the result immediately, especially when that result is safe, reliable power for the people who depend on it. That is what drew me to becoming an electrician: the practical challenge of finding faults, putting them right, and knowing that reliable power improves everyday life in direct, meaningful ways. What began as a fascination with how things work has grown into a career focused on keeping homes, businesses, and people connected. I am originally from the Netherlands, and I bring to my work the same commitment to steady progress that supported me through a Doctorate at a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my career, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing how much I value work that can be seen, tested, and relied upon. One of my favourite family memories is showing a relative a building I had helped wire, only for the lights to come on just as I explained my role; it turned an ordinary moment into a lasting reminder that this job creates something real.

My professional foundation has been built through practical electrical work and continued learning. When I needed to use a new diagnostic tool and become familiar with a related technical area, I did not master it overnight; instead, I built confidence over more than a year of regular use on routine jobs until it became part of my normal working practice. In day-to-day fault-finding, I work carefully through established procedures to identify and resolve issues safely and efficiently, and when an unusual case falls outside the normal pattern, I make a point of seeking guidance before proceeding. That approach has helped me diagnose faults quickly and accurately while keeping downtime to a minimum. At the same time, colleagues have occasionally come to me with questions in my own area, such as checking a testing sequence or confirming the likely cause of a recurring fault, and I have been glad to talk it through with them. I am now eager to bring this practical mindset, grounded training, and genuine enthusiasm for electrical work to my next role as an electrician.

A strong visual identity can change the way people feel, understand, and connect long before a single word is read. It is this belief that drew me to graphic design and continues to shape the way I approach creative work: I want to produce visuals that are not only striking, but purposeful and memorable. Originally from Peru, I built my academic foundation through a Doctorate at a university ranked in the global top 100, an experience that strengthened the research, structure, and disciplined thinking I bring to creative projects. Across my work, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each requiring me to turn broad concepts into clear visual systems that could work consistently across print, digital, and brand touchpoints. In particular, I became increasingly interested in how abstract ideas can be distilled into cohesive identities that people immediately recognise and respond to, which confirmed for me that graphic design was the right professional path.

Alongside this, I have learned to adapt quickly in practical settings. On one project, I needed to use a new design tool that the team had recently adopted; within a few weeks I was using it confidently in live work, and soon after that I was helping colleagues get started when they asked how to handle layouts and shared assets. In another role, repeated delays were being caused by a file-handoff issue between design and production, so I set up a simpler naming and export process that reduced confusion and helped the team move work forward more smoothly. I also value working closely with others and sharing knowledge in a straightforward way when it is useful.

Beyond my academic and professional development, one of my favourite memories came during a family visit to a local café where I had recently redesigned the branding. My family immediately pointed out the menu, signage, and packaging before I said anything, and seeing them interact so naturally with something I had created reminded me that good design becomes part of everyday life. Altogether, these experiences have prepared me to contribute thoughtfully as a Graphic Designer while continuing to grow through purposeful, engaging visual communication.

Reliable results often depend on work that happens quietly, carefully, and with full respect for process, and that is exactly what draws me to laboratory work. My natural curiosity about how things work, combined with a desire to contribute to accurate, meaningful results, has led me toward a career as a Laboratory Technician, where careful testing supports wider scientific and healthcare goals. I am especially motivated by the idea that precision behind the scenes can make a real difference in research, quality, and patient outcomes. This aligns closely with the way I like to work: maintaining accuracy under pressure, whether preparing samples or documenting results with consistency and care so that the wider team can rely on each stage of testing. Therefore, I seek to build on my foundation through practical laboratory work informed by my Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, with the long-term goal of contributing to dependable testing and high-quality scientific outcomes. Originally from Ethiopia, I bring that background as part of my personal journey while grounding my professional focus firmly in the laboratory environment.

I have been fortunate to grow in an environment where careful work and genuine enthusiasm could be shared at home as well as at work. One of my favourite family memories is coming home after a busy week in the lab and discovering that my younger sibling had turned our kitchen into a “mini lab,” carefully labelling cups of juice like test samples; it was a funny but proud reminder that my connection to methodical work and discovery was visible to my family too. In my professional experience, I completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of dependable processes and clear results.
